papers.title: Effect of Laser Power on the Corrosion and Wear Resistance of Laser Cladding TC4 Alloy
papers.abstract: TC4 alloy coatings were fabricated on a titanium alloy substrate using laser cladding. The influence of laser power ranging from 1000 W to 2200 W on the microhardness, wear resistance, and electrochemical corrosion behavior in 3.5% NaCl solution was systematically investigated. Results demonstrate that the TC4 coating exhibited a 35.17% enhancement in microhardness compared to the substrate, with an average value reaching 500 HV. As the laser power increased from 1000 W to 2200 W, the maximum wear depth progressively decreased, indicating significantly improved wear resistance, with fatigue wear being identified as the dominant mechanism. The coating prepared at 1400 W showed the best corrosion performance, displaying the highest self-corrosion potential of −0.110 V, the lowest corrosion current density of 0.125 μA·cm−2, and the largest polarization resistance of 2.057 × 106 Ω·cm2. The charge transfer resistance initially increased and then decreased with increasing laser power. Numerical simulations revealed that when exposed to seawater, galvanic couples formed between the α and β phases on the TC4 titanium alloy surface, resulting in preferential dissolution of the β-phase.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要研究激光熔覆TC4涂层的腐蚀和磨损性能，而非基体金属的力学或疲劳性能，与用户关注的Ti-6Al-4V机械/疲劳方向相关性低。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on corrosion and wear resistance of laser-cladded TC4 coatings, with no testing or modeling of tensile, ductility, or fatigue properties as required by the direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究激光功率对激光熔覆TC4合金涂层腐蚀和磨损性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 在不同激光功率（1000-2200 W）下制备TC4涂层，进行微观硬度、磨损和电化学腐蚀测试。
summary_zh.result: 1400 W时腐蚀性能最优，耐磨性随功率增加而提升，疲劳磨损为主机制。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验测试和数值模拟验证涂层性能。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of laser power on the corrosion and wear resistance of laser-cladded TC4 alloy coatings.
summary_en.method: TC4 coatings were fabricated at laser powers from 1000 W to 2200 W and characterized for microhardness, wear, and electrochemical corrosion in 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary_en.result: The coating at 1400 W exhibited the best corrosion resistance, while higher laser power improved wear resistance via fatigue wear mechanism.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements and numerical simulations of galvanic corrosion between α and β phases.
